title: Homemade Pizza
metaDescription: Homemade pizza with a crispy crust, tangy sauce and melted mozzarella — better than delivery, made in your own oven.
author: Laura Bennett
keywords: homemade pizza, pizza dough recipe, easy homemade pizza
ingredients: 1 lb pizza dough (store-bought or homemade), room temperature
Toppings of choice (pepperoni, mushrooms, peppers, etc.)

steps.name: Preheat
steps.text: Preheat oven to 475°F (245°C) with a pizza stone or baking sheet inside to heat up.

steps.name: Shape the dough
steps.text: On a lightly floured surface, stretch or roll the dough into a 12-inch round. Transfer to a pizza peel or parchment paper dusted with cornmeal.

steps.name: Add toppings
steps.text: Brush the edges with olive oil. Spread pizza sauce evenly, leaving a border for the crust. Top with mozzarella and desired toppings, then sprinkle with oregano.

steps.name: Bake
steps.text: Slide the pizza onto the hot stone or baking sheet. Bake for 12-15 minutes until the crust is golden and the cheese is bubbly and lightly browned.

tips.question: Why preheat the pizza stone or pan?
tips.answer: A hot surface gives the dough an immediate blast of heat from underneath, which is what creates a crispy crust bottom — putting dough on a cold pan results in a pale, soft base.

tips.question: Why let the dough come to room temperature first?
tips.answer: Cold dough straight from the fridge is stiff and resists stretching, tearing easily — room temperature dough is far more pliable and easier to shape without holes.

tips.question: How do I avoid a soggy center?
tips.answer: Don't overload with sauce or watery toppings (like fresh tomato slices) — use a moderate amount of sauce and pat very wet toppings dry before adding them.

storyIntro: Homemade pizza gets better the moment you start preheating the pan or stone along with the oven — that blast of bottom heat is the difference between a crispy crust and a soggy one.
Beyond that, it's just assembly, and it's faster than waiting for delivery most nights.
storyNote: Preheat the stone or pan along with the oven for the full time — sliding dough onto a surface that hasn't had time to get hot is the most common reason homemade pizza crust turns out pale and soft.
